To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified seven novel mutations in FXIII‐A subunit gene in 10 unrelated patients with FXIII deficiency, including a compound heterozygotus and four homozygotes.
we identified seven novel mutations in the FXIIIIA gene in 10 unrelated patients with FXIII deficiency.
we have identified seven novel mutations in FXIIIA gene in 10 unrelated Jewish, Arab and Indian families.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis of FXIII‐A deficiency in the Israeli and Indian Jewish communities and in a Tunisian family.
the molecular basis of hereditary F XIII deficiency and the identification of novel mutations in FXIII‐deficient families of different origins.
the identification of seven novel FXIII A‐subunit mutations in 10 unrelated patients from Israel, India, and Tunisia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all the mutations are likely to be deleterious and result in FXIII deficiency.
the new mutations identified in this study cause severe FXIII deficiency and are responsible for the bleeding diathesis in the patients.
all novel mutations cause severe FXIII deficiency and are expected to be associated with a bleeding phenotype.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the new missense mutation Gly210Arg is likely to cause protein misfunding and the other three missense mutations are likely to impair catalytic process or stability of the protein.
seven new mutations in the FXIIIIA gene were identified in 10 unrelated patients from Israel, Tunisia and India.

seven novel mutations in FXIIIA gene were identified, and the structural analysis of the mutations suggested that the mutations are likely to cause protein misfunding and/or impairment of catalytic process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FXIII A‐subunit deficiency is a heterogeneous bleeding disorder with a wide spectrum of mutations.
the FXIII A gene is a hot spot for mutations and that the mutations identified in this gene are mostly of the missense type.
mutations in the A subunit of FXIII are diverse and that the mutations can be identified in all the exons.
